This implies a potential role for Timolol in modulating neural activity associated with migraine, possibly through its effects on the autonomic nervous system. The shared ontological category of beta-adrenergic antagonists and the indirect link from Timolol to migraine via propranolol highlight a possible pharmacological relationship that warrants further investigation. The evidence supports a mechanism where Timolol, as a beta-adrenergic antagonist, may influence migraine pathways through its effects on vascular and neural systems, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated.
